=== 6 guidance rules for: Review additive SQLite migration receipt retry and rollback with immutable authorization provenance and private versus public DTO validation (project ops-desk) ===

[1] SQLite-first persistence (better-sqlite3/Drizzle or sqlite-vec); not Postgres by default  (STRONG, data-storage, mona/farha/strike/supermag/xml)
    ✅ Use SQLite as the primary store (sqlite-vec for vectors). For concurrency set WAL + busy_timeout and read SQLite concurrency docs via context7. One .db file on the server/VPS is acceptable. (EduBlend is the deliberate exception: it uses Neon Postgres.)
    ❌ Reach for Postgres/Neon/Mongo/Turso by default because the project started on Vercel; treat SQLite as a cache layer.
[2] Multi-tenant via per-tenant SQLite; tilitoimisto shares one DB, independents get their own (migrate on independence)  (STRONG, multi-tenant, xml/farha)
    ✅ Each school/independent company gets its own SQLite file; a tilitoimisto + its client companies share one SQLite; a separate control.db holds the superadmin/tenant registry. When a client goes independent, migrate its data to its own SQLite. (DB-per-tenant = natural GDPR isolation.)
    ❌ One shared DB with a tenant_id column for everyone, or every company its own DB from day one regardless of relationship.
[3] B2B/institutional: invite-only auth, no public self-serve signup, external invoicing (no Stripe checkout)  (STRONG, multi-tenant, strike/edu-blend)
    ✅ Invite-only: superadmin → org (gym/school/tilitoimisto) → coaches/teachers → learners. Sales-led for enterprises/governments/institutions; reps send invoices; billing is external. Sandbox is for gated evaluation.
    ❌ Public signup page/open registration; Stripe self-serve checkout; docs assuming open-source self-onboarding ('fork the repo', free tier).
[4] Know each project's deploy target; persistent-volume servers (Railway/Hetzner/VPS) over Vercel when a SQLite volume is needed  (STRONG, infra-deploy, farha/edu-blend/strike/supermag)
    ✅ Match the project: farha→Railway; EduBlend→Railway backend + Vercel frontend (sandbox + prod); strike→Hetzner; supermag→VPS. Use that platform's CLI; Vercel's serverless model can't host a persistent SQLite volume. After every merge, verify backend (railway logs/status) and frontend (vercel) builds before live tests.
    ❌ Assume Vercel; confuse which platform is in use; assume the deploy succeeded without checking the build log.
[5] Finnish/marketing copy: no dashes, no jargon, understated; run adversarial review before commit  (STRONG, finnish-language, xml/strike)
    ✅ Plain, understated copy with specific facts not declarations; say 'viranomaisilmoitukset' over naming services; research copyschool/conversion frameworks. Run reviewer sub-agents (copy-critic, Finnish proofreader, IP/accuracy auditor) before committing; on 529 errors retry, don't commit unreviewed.
    ❌ Use em/en dashes; name technical formats (camt.053, CSV) or authorities (OmaVero, Tulorekisteri); state obvious self-evident claims ('KPL/VAT compliant'); write generic copy; ship unreviewed.
[6] Strict TDD: write failing tests first (confirm RED), then implement; tests must trace to the code change  (STRONG, testing-verification, supermag/edu-blend)
    ✅ Write tests verbatim from the plan, run and confirm RED, then implement and report RED→GREEN. Add defensive edge-case tests beyond the plan (plan is a floor, not a ceiling). Every test change must be traceable to a code change and must fail when the code is reverted.
    ❌ Write impl and tests together or tests after; skip the explicit RED step; edit assertions to go green without tying them to a real code change.
